name: Nox
description: Canonical token source for the Nox Jellyfin theme. Every colour, radius, duration and metric the theme uses is declared here once and consumed by nox.css. Nothing is estimated: each entry names the rule that declares it and the selectors in nox.css that read it.

conventions.definedIn: The selector whose rule block declares the custom property. `:root` is the default palette; `.nox-*` is an alternate.
conventions.usedIn: Representative selectors in nox.css that consume the property. Not exhaustive — it shows each token's design intent.
conventions.values: Custom properties are consumed with var(). Where a property is read back inside a colour function, an -rgb triplet exists alongside it so the alpha channel can be varied.
conventions.headerSelectors: Header rules in nox.css are written `body .skinHeader ...`. The `body` prefix lifts them above Jellyfin's own equal-specificity rules so the theme does not depend on which stylesheet the browser parses last. The selectors above are quoted in their short form for readability.

surface.note: Page field. A warm near-black, not a neutral one — it keeps black artwork from looking pasted onto the page.
Optional top-of-page wash. Sits under everything and is removed in light palettes where it would read as a smudge.
True black, used for the one element that should read as a physical object: the floating navigation rail, the hero's action plaque, and modal chrome.
One step above black, for panels that sit on --nox-bg rather than over artwork.

line.note: Hairline. Alpha, not a solid grey, so it composites correctly over artwork as well as flat surfaces.

text.note: Primary copy. Pure white is deliberate: it is only ever used over black or a scrimmed image.
Muted blue-grey. Carries headings and metadata that should recede without losing legibility.
Lowest tier. Long-form synopsis and inactive control glyphs only.

accent.note: The single brand colour. Changing this one property re-skins every accent surface in the theme.
Triplet form so tints can be built with rgba() at any alpha without a second literal colour.
Foreground for anything filled with the accent. Gold cannot carry white text at any size.
Keyboard focus. Translucent so it reads as a halo over both flat panels and artwork.

radius.note: Posters. Mirrored into Jellyfin's own --jf-card-borderRadius so React-rendered cards match.
Small controls. Deliberately tighter than the card radius so buttons do not read as chips.
The hero frame. Large radius is what separates the hero from the page rather than a border.
The action strip inside the hero.

metric.note: Gutter between posters in a row.
Navigation rail at rest. The page's left padding is derived from this, so the rail can never overlap content.
Rail on hover or keyboard focus, wide enough for the longest Jellyfin header label without truncation.
Gap between the rail and the viewport edge. The rail floats; it is never flush.
The pill. Softer than a card, tighter than the hero.

motion.note: Default for anything that moves a short distance.
Rail expansion. Shorter than the eye expects a panel to take, long enough to read as motion rather than a jump.
Opacity and colour. A plain ease is invisible at these durations and costs nothing.
Anything that changes size or position: fast out of the gate, settled at the end.

depth.note: Backdrop-filter radius where blur is supported.
Hover lift only. The resting poster has no shadow, which is what keeps a row of twelve of them from looking noisy.
The rail floats above the page, so it needs a shadow on all sides rather than a border-bottom.

type.value: "Roboto Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace
type.note: Metadata, numeric readouts and secondary controls. The web font is not loaded by default; see tokens.css for the opt-in @import.

type.value: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
type.note: Titles. A system stack on purpose: it renders instantly, needs no network, and cannot be a blocker on a login screen.

jellyfinBridge.note: Jellyfin's React UI reads MUI custom properties rather than the theme's. These map Nox values onto them. The names are version-specific and are the first thing to check if a Jellyfin update renders something unthemed.

palettes.label: Nox Light
palettes.note: Also sets color-scheme: light so form controls and scrollbars follow. on-accent is black rather than white: white on #b8860b measures 3.25:1 and fails AA for the button labels placed on it; black measures 6.45:1.

palettes.label: Nox Oyster
palettes.note: Also sets color-scheme: light so form controls and scrollbars follow. on-accent is black: 6.45:1 against 3.25:1 for white.

palettes.label: Nox Arctic Dawn
palettes.note: Also sets color-scheme: light so form controls and scrollbars follow. on-accent is black: 5.71:1 against 3.68:1 for white.

palettes.label: Nox Enterprise Light
palettes.note: Also sets color-scheme: light so form controls and scrollbars follow.

contrast.method: WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance ratio, computed from the hex values above.

defaultPalette.level: AA large text and non-text UI only

contrast.note: --nox-muted clears AA for large text and for non-text UI, which is the whole of its job: synopsis paragraphs at 16px and above, and inactive icon glyphs. It is never used for a control label or small body copy. Every other pair in the default palette clears AAA. In the lighter palettes --nox-muted is the tightest pair at 3.31:1 (nox-oyster) and should not be pushed any lighter.

notes: Nox consumes every token through var(); no component in nox.css holds a literal colour. Re-declaring a token on a more specific selector retints the theme without touching a layout rule.
Four of the light palettes also redeclare --nox-border and --nox-border-strong, because the default hairline is a light alpha that disappears against white.

Three light palettes declare a black --nox-on-accent where an earlier draft used white. White on those accents measured 3.25:1 to 3.68:1, which fails AA for the button labels that sit on the accent fill. The ratios in `contrast` above are the post-fix values.
Colours that vary with hover are derived with color-mix() or rgba(var(--nox-accent-rgb), a) rather than declared as a second literal, so a palette swap cannot leave a stale hover colour behind.

The --jf-* properties are a compatibility bridge, not a token. They exist because Jellyfin's React layer reads MUI variables instead of the theme's own, and they are the one group here that may need adjusting after a Jellyfin upgrade.
